item: A write-gate waiter looks again every second, so a wake-up lost in release (or in the finally of a gave-up acquire) costs one step and not the rest of the process
refs: open item L2 of PR #1435; coordinator 17 Oct (order: M, the D note, L2)
summary: WriterGate.release clears the owner and then wakes the head of the queue; a KeyboardInterrupt or MemoryError inside that wake-up (forced in the new test on the real release) left the gate free and the head asleep on a condition nobody notifies, and acquire's wait had no timeout, so every later writer queued behind it until restart. acquire now waits in steps of _WAKE_STEP_S (1.0 s, chosen, not tuned: nothing measured argues for it over 0.25 or 2): untimed waits step by it, bounded waits by min(time left, step), in the same loop shape the interrupt pins check. Not a timeout (an acquire without one waits as long as the gate is held; pinned) and a bounded acquire still gives up at its own deadline. Cost measured: 49 queued writers behind a 20 s hold, 0.0002 s CPU before and 0.0366 s after (980 wake-ups, about 37 us each, 0.18 percent of a core). Red-without: on the gate as it was both injection tests fail (the writer never gets through) and the pin fails; a control with the step stubbed out leaves the writer asleep. Named: a failure in the wake-up skips the measuring of that one release; the real-signal rate of the loss was not measured.
